explanation: Gauchos, the cowboys of Argentina and Uruguay, herded cattle across these plains, whose deep, rich soils make superb farmland.

claims.text: The vast, flat grasslands of Argentina are called the Pampas.
The steppe is Eurasian grassland, the prairie North American grassland and the savanna tropical grassland.
Gauchos, the horsemen of Argentina and Uruguay, herded cattle on the Pampas.
The Pampas have deep, fertile soils that make excellent farmland.

evidence.restatement: The vast flat grasslands of Argentina are the Pampas.
The steppe is Eurasian grassland, the prairie North American grassland and the savanna tropical grassland.
Gauchos, the horsemen of Argentina and Uruguay, herded cattle on the Pampas.
The Pampas have deep, fertile soils that make them prime farmland.
The Pampas are the vast, flat, fertile grasslands of Argentina (and Uruguay and southern Brazil).
The steppe is the temperate grassland of Eurasia, the prairie that of North America, and the savanna tropical grassland.
Gauchos are the horsemen and cattle herders of the Pampas in Argentina and Uruguay.
The Pampas have deep, fertile soils that suit farming.

issues.note: Argentina also has the Patagonian steppe, so 'The Steppe' is not absurd as a lure. The key stays unique because the stem's 'vast, flat grasslands' describes the Pampas, Patagonia is semi-arid shrub steppe on plateaus, and 'the steppe' normally means the Eurasian one (claim c2 says so).
